small_guidance: The matmul kernel itself is fine; the correctness bug is in the Linear replacement path. For nn.Linear (e.g. lm_head), the weight is tied to wte and shape is [vocab, hidden]; doing weight.data.t().contiguous() creates a new tensor and breaks weight tying. Also, GPT-2's lm_head is an nn.Linear with no bias that shares wte.weight — replacing it after .cuda() with a transposed copy desynchronizes from embeddings. Fix: skip lm_head or handle weight-tying explicitly, and verify the Conv1D weight layout (Conv1D stores weight as [in, out] already, so passing child.weight directly is correct). Add an atol-tolerant numeric check by comparing a single block first.
large_guidance: Redesign the replacement pass to be type- and tying-aware: (1) detect tied weights (lm_head.weight is wte.weight) and either leave lm_head as PyTorch F.linear against the live embedding matrix, or implement it as a triton matmul that reads wte.weight directly without copying; (2) for Conv1D use weight as-is ([in,out]); for nn.Linear use weight.t() via stride manipulation (no .contiguous() copy) so tying is preserved; (3) keep accumulation in fp32 but cast inputs/weights consistent with the model dtype; (4) consider fusing the final LayerNorm + lm_head matmul, and fusing bias+GELU for the MLP fc layer to reduce memory traffic.
